title: Onboarding oracle + shadow-traffic verification for publishing performance signatures
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: build an "onboarding oracle" that validates a candidate model's Redwood-verified performance signature using sampled shadow traffic before publishing and pinning a profile. The oracle runs candidate variants in dry-run / shadow mode alongside production, collects latency/throughput/cost signals, compares statistically to a reference signature, and emits a signed attestation or rejects the publish. This reduces post-publish regressions and automates rollback triggers for profile pinning.

Scope: 
- Shadow traffic harness in staging and optional production-safe sampling.
- Oracle service to ingest metrics, run statistical tests, and produce pass/fail + confidence intervals.
- Integration with the profile registry and publish pipeline to attach attestations and rollback hooks.
- Dashboards and alerts for failed validations and drift.

Out of scope for this ticket: end-to-end customer migration for pinned profiles, full legal attestation flows, and advanced cost normalization (separate follow-up).
background: We have recurring incidents where a 'verified' performance profile, once pinned, later shows regressions for certain workloads (long-tail latency, batch-specific inefficiencies). Existing validation relies on synthetic benchmarks and small-scale canaries. Shadowing real traffic provides a higher-fidelity signal while preserving safety. Engineering has prototype infra to shadow requests (ENG-12234) but lacks an automated gating oracle and signed attestation artifacts to attach to published profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle service accepts a candidate model/version and a reference performance signature and returns a pass/fail decision with confidence metrics.
Shadow traffic harness delivers sampled production-like requests to candidate variants without affecting live responses (drop-and-observe).
Profile publish pipeline stores a signed attestation artifact when oracle passes and blocks publish when oracle fails, surfacing clear reasons in the UI.
Dashboards show per-profile drift metrics, delta distributions, and automated alerting for >P95 latency regressions or >10% cost increase vs baseline.
Playbook documented: how to interpret oracle failures, manual override process, and rollback steps for pinned profiles.
plan: Week 1: finalize oracle validation criteria (statistical tests, thresholds, sampling rates) with Eng and SRE.
Week 2: implement lightweight oracle microservice; wire metrics ingestion (latency, throughput, token-cost estimates).
Week 3: integrate shadow harness (use ENG-12234 hook), run smoke validations with internal canaries, add signed attestation artifact generation.
Week 4: connect oracle to profile publish pipeline, add UI indicators in Console, and create alerting dashboards (CloudWatch/Grafana).
Week 5: run staged onboarding for 2 candidate models, collect results, refine thresholds, and finalize runbook.
tasks: PM: finalize validation policy and acceptance criteria (Aisha).
ENG: wire shadow traffic harness and ensure no user-facing degradation (SRE + Runtime).
ENG: implement signed attestation artifact storage (Registry team).
DX/Console: surface publish decisions and failure reasons in Profile publish flow.
SRE: create dashboards + alert rules for drift and regression signals.
Legal/Security: light review of attestation artifact format (informational).
QA: run end-to-end smoke tests with synthetic and shadowed traffic.
